text: 25 YEARS. WE WILL NEVER FORGET.[image]AFGHANISTAN[image][image]At the end of a beautiful day here on Cape Cod, we pause and remember.[image][image]Twenty-five years ago today, the war in Afghanistan began. For 20 years, brave Americans and our allies served, sacrificed, and answered the call.[image][image]We remember those who made the ultimate sacrifice, like Nicholas. We remember those who were wounded. We remember the families who lost husbands, wives, sons and daughters.[image][image]But we also want to remember all those who came home and continue to serve.[image][image]They are all around us. They are police officers and firefighters. They are teachers, mechanics, business owners, fathers, mothers and neighbors. They continue to serve their communities and make a difference every day.[image][image]To every Afghanistan veteran: You served. You sacrificed. You made a difference. Be proud of your service, because we are forever proud of you.[image]🇺🇸🙏🏻🫡[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmericans #Afghanistan #USA #HonorAndRespect #LivingTheDream [image]The Nicholas G. FOR SEAN[image]Day Two and Graduation Day at the K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon Training Center in Yarmouth. What a great day to be back at the house that Sean built.[image][image]After two days of intense, hands-on training, we celebrated the graduation of an incredible group of police officers who stepped up to learn and sharpen their skills as K9 decoys. This training is so important to building safe, effective K9 teams and preparing these officers and dogs for the challenges they face protecting our communities.[image][image]Congratulations to our graduating officers:[image][image]Sean Lowe — Falmouth Police Department[image]Kevin Lynch — Cohasset Police Department[image]Brandon Sanders — Barnstable Police Department[image]Dan Ruth — Barnstable Police Department[image]Richard Proctor — Plymouth County Sheriff’s Office[image]Glenn Haley — Plymouth County Sheriff’s Office[image]Joe Silva — Plymouth County Sheriff’s Office[image]Bryan Lobianco — Hingham Police Department[image]Andrew Latosek — Medway Police Department[image]Liam Breen — Yarmouth Police Department[image]Bryan Derochea — Mashpee Police Department[image]Brian Smith — West Bridgewater Police Department[image][image]Thank you to the instructors, the participating departments, and everyone who made these two days of training and today’s graduation possible. The dedication of these officers is impressive, and these K9s are absolutely amazing.[image][image]Our family is proud to help make this training possible through a $5,000 grant from Big Nick’s Ride and the Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund, in memory of our son Nick and in memory of the son of our good friends Denise and Patrick Gannon.[image][image]Sean dreamed of building a place where K9 teams could train and become better prepared to protect others. Seeing that dream continue to make a difference, and knowing that Nick’s legacy is helping support these officers, means more than words can say.[image][image]Congratulations to all 12 graduates. Thank you for your commitment to serving and protecting others.[image][image]We will always Back the Blue. We will continue doing everything we can to support our police officers and K9 teams with the training and equipment they need to do their jobs safely and effectively.[image][image]Pain to purpose. FOR SEAN[image]What an incredible day back in Yarmouth at the K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon Training Center — the house that Sean built.[image][image]Today’s state-of-the-art K9 training brought together incredible police officers and some truly incredible dogs. There is so much that goes into properly training a K9 team, including teaching officers how to safely serve as decoys and teaching these dogs how to properly bite, hold and release.[image][image]These officers are committed to doing the job right, and these dogs are absolutely amazing.[image][image]Our family is proud to be in a position to help provide this training through a $5,000 grant from Big Nick’s Ride and the Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund, in memory Nick, and in memory of the son of our good friends, Denise and Patrick Gannon.[image][image]Sean Gannon. Nick Xiarhos. Two sons. Two fallen heroes. [image][image]There is something very powerful about seeing the legacy of these young men helping protect the men and women who put their lives on the line every day.[image][image]We will always Back the Blue, and we will do everything we can to help provide our police officers and K9 teams with the training and equipment they need to do their jobs safely and effectively.[image][image]Pain to purpose. GOOD MORNING & HAPPY THANKFUL THURSDAY [image]Operation Flags for Vets[image][image]Today we are especially thankful for the Monti family and the incredible tradition they continue to carry on in honor of their son and brother, U.S. Army Sergeant Jared C. Monti—a Medal of Honor recipient—our nations highest honor. [image][image]Jared was born and raised right here in Massachusetts and gave his life serving our country in Afghanistan. His incredibly strong and proud father, Paul Monti, turned his unimaginable loss into a lasting mission of love, remembrance and service.[image][image]That mission became Operation Flags for Vets.[image][image]Twice a year, during Veterans Day week and Memorial Day week, volunteers gather at our Massachusetts National Cemetery in Bourne to place American flags on the graves of our fallen heroes.[image][image]People come from all over. Young and old. Veterans, families, friends and complete strangers. They walk among the graves, place a flag, and say the name of the hero who rests there.[image][image]That is what makes this tradition so powerful.[image][image]It reminds us that these men and women are not forgotten.[image][image]As the years have gone by, the tradition continues. The Monti family continues to lead, and thousands of people continue to show up to honor Jared and every hero who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country.[image][image]Flag Placement Day is November 7th at 9:00 AM.[image]Flag Pickup Day is November 14th at 9:00 AM.[image][image]We hope to see you there.[image][image]God bless the Monti Gold Star family, every Gold Star family who carries this loss every single day, and all those who have served, all those who continue to serve, and every volunteer who takes the time to place and retrieve these flags.[image][image]Happy Thankful Thursday, Cape Cod. [image][image]See you on November 7th and 14th. GOOD MORNING AND HAPPY REMEMBER EVERYONE DEPLOYED FRIDAY![image][image]FROM TRAGEDY TO TRIUMPH![image][image]Some GREAT NEWS to share![image][image]My good friend James LaMonte and his team at the K9 PTSD Center in Seekonk continue to do incredible work for our four-legged heroes.[image][image]The new Massachusetts K9 license plates are arriving! Thousands have been ordered, and you’ll be seeing them all over the Commonwealth.[image][image]The plates feature K9 Nero, a Belgian Malinois, with the letters SG honoring Sergeant Sean Gannon. They also recognize K9 Mikey, a retired Boston Police K9 German Shepherd who was James LaMonte’s first dog.[image][image]The money raised helps support the dogs at the Seekonk center and the planned second Canine PTSD Center right here in Bourne on Cape Cod![image][image]And don’t forget, we hold an annual blood drive for dogs in Sean’s memory. Best of all, Nero is still alive and STILL RUNNING STRONG![image][image]Please join us October 18th in Bourne for the first-ever K9 5K on Cape Cod! We’ll recognize the incredible K9 heroes and their handlers from across the Commonwealth, and we hope to make it an annual tradition.[image][image]Think about how far we’ve come since the tragic loss of Sean Gannon and the shooting of his devoted partner, Nero.[image][image]We’ve built the K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon Training Center at Yarmouth Police Headquarters, Sean’s dream. We’ve passed Nero’s Law and Dakota’s Law, established a nonprofit in Sean’s memory, organized an annual K9 blood drive, and now have these new license plates. And there’s so much more to come![image][image]Sometimes, when horrible things happen, we look for a reason why. Sometimes, we have to turn that tragedy into something that helps others and makes a difference. And that’s exactly what we’re doing.[image][image]I think about Sean’s parents, Denise and Patrick, his wife Dara, his siblings, and all their family and friends. Can you imagine what it must mean to see all the good that has come from Sean’s life and sacrifice?[image][image]From saving dogs to training officers, these four-legged heroes serve alongside our military, police, and corrections officers. Dogs like Nero, Thor, Dakota, Kitt, Frankie, and so many others deserve our support.[image][image]Sean’s legacy lives on. And it doesn’t stop here. It never will.[image][image]Remember Everyone Deployed. Give your dog an extra treat, and keep an eye out for the new K9 license plates on vehicles all over the Commonwealth![image]🇺🇸💙🐕👏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #K9 #BackTheBlue #NerosLaw #DakotasLaw #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MAPolice #ForSean[image]K9 PTSD Center[image]Healing Dakota[image]Rehoboth K9 Edo[image]Barnstable Police K9 Foundation[image]K9 Flexx and Retired/Police K9 Mr. Warner.[image]K9 Kitt Foundation[image]K9 Hurricane's Heroes[image]The Plymouth County Sheriff's Department[image]Riptide K-9[image]State Representative Justin Thurber[image]Senator Kelly Dooner[image]Cape Cod Realtor Lori Jurkowski[image]Support Our Troops - Wear Red Friday's[image]Modern Primitive K9[image]Denise Morency Gannon
